title: Ordinary mind
hook: Zhaozhou asks Nanquan what the way is: ordinary mind is the way (Gateless Gate 19)
carry: nothing useless clings to the mind

segments.voice: Yesterday: Yunmen, and your line, this one is it. Today closes the week with the plainest koan of all.

People go a long way looking for the spiritual life. Retreats in the mountains. A trip to India. A new book every month, each promising what the last one didn't quite deliver. There's nothing wrong with any of it. But sometimes the looking itself keeps you from finding. Before Zhaozhou was the old master of mu and the washed bowl, he was a young monk with a big question. He took it to his teacher Nanquan, the same Nanquan from the cat. The answer is very short.
screen: `RETREATS, TRIPS, A BOOK EVERY MONTH.` → `THE LOOKING THAT KEEPS YOU FROM FINDING.` → `YOUNG ZHAOZHOU'S QUESTION.`

segments.voice: Zhaozhou asked: what is the Way? Nanquan said: ordinary mind is the Way. Zhaozhou pressed: then should I aim myself toward it? Nanquan: the moment you aim at it, you turn away from it. Zhaozhou: but if I don't aim at it, how will I know it's the Way? Nanquan: the Way isn't a matter of knowing or not knowing. Knowing is a kind of illusion; not knowing is just a blank. When you really reach the Way beyond doubt, it's wide open, like the sky. Why insist on right and wrong? And the case says Zhaozhou woke up. Ordinary mind isn't a dull mind or a lazy one. It's the mind you already have, before you start trying to become someone more spiritual: getting up, eating, walking, washing the bowl. Wumen's verse goes, roughly: spring has its flowers, autumn its moon, summer its cool breeze, winter its snow. If nothing useless clings to the mind, that's the good season of a life. Look back at the week. Juzhi's finger: your own finger. The flag and the wind: mind moves. The flower sermon: the smile. Original face, before you were born. Nanquan's cat, sandals on the head. Every day is a good day. And now the plainest: ordinary mind. Almost every story this week pointed away from somewhere else and back to right here.
screen: `WHAT IS THE WAY?` · `AIM AT IT AND YOU TURN AWAY.` · `WIDE OPEN, LIKE THE SKY.` · `FLOWERS, MOON, BREEZE, SNOW.` · then, large: `ORDINARY MIND.`

segments.voice: Don't try to meditate well; just sit the way you'd sit waiting for the kettle, noticing the weight of your body, the sound of the room, the breath doing what it always does. There's no special state to reach. If you catch yourself aiming at something, let the aim drop and come back to plain sitting.
Ordinary mind. Nanquan's answer to what the Way is: the mind you already have, before you aim at something special.
Your line: nothing useless clings to the mind. Spring flowers, autumn moon, and this plain day too. That closes the week.

howItsDone: Zen communities treat daily tasks such as cooking, cleaning and gardening as practice, and Wumen's verse on the four seasons from this case is often quoted and brushed as calligraphy.

original.note: Chinese píngcháng xīn shì dào: ordinary mind is the Way.

what a scholar hears: the saying goes back to Nanquan's own teacher Mazu Daoyi, and the case is Gateless Gate 19, with Wumen's four-seasons verse.
